title: Microsoft Dataverse: Python SDK for scripting and agent workflows
summary: The roadmap details and SDK capabilities are supported, but two automation entries only read settings rather than configure the controls they accompany. Replace those read operations with documented update operations before administrators rely on the controls table.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SDK is published under open-source licensing.
claims.quote: The SDK for Python is published under open-source licensing.

claims.claim: The SDK lets Python developers and data scientists manipulate Dataverse data without .NET knowledge.
claims.quote: You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse by using familiar Python syntax. You don't need any .NET knowledge.

claims.claim: Developers install the PyPI package with pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client.
claims.quote:
This command installs the latest stable release of the SDK from a pypi.org package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client

claims.claim: Learn also documents installation from the GitHub source repository.
claims.quote: Run the following command to install the SDK from the project's GitHub source instead of from the package.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the item as enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

claims.claim: The getting-started page requires Python 3.10+.
claims.quote: An activated Python 3.10+ environment.

claims.claim: The reference-architecture page instead requires Python 3.13 or later.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites

Access to a Power Platform environment with Dataverse
Appropriate security roles
Python 3.13 or later

claims.claim: The SDK supports create, retrieve, update and delete data operations.
claims.quote: CRUD operations | Support for create, retrieve, update, and delete data operations by using a single request.

claims.claim: Bulk creation uses CreateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: Bulk updates use UpdateMultiple.
claims.quote: This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Bulk upserts use UpsertMultiple.
claims.quote: A single item uses a PATCH request while multiple items use the UpsertMultiple bulk action.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SDK can delete many rows through BulkDelete in a single service call.
claims.quote: Specify multiple operations in a single web service call. This feature uses Dataverse's native CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple, and BulkDelete Web API operations

claims.claim: The SDK supports read-only direct SQL SELECT queries.
claims.quote: Direct-SQL queries | Supports simple read-only "SELECT" statements with paging.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The SDK provides pandas DataFrame wrappers and can extract tables into DataFrames.
claims.quote: Client wrappers are provided for all CRUD operations where DataFrames and Series data types are returned to the caller.

claims.claim: The SDK uploads files to Dataverse file columns.
claims.quote: File operations | Upload files to a Dataverse file column with automatic chunking for large files.

claims.claim: The SDK supports batch requests.
claims.quote: Batch operations | Send multiple CRUD, table metadata, and SQL query operations in a single HTTP request with optional transactional changesets.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SDK can create, update and delete custom tables.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The SDK can create, update and delete custom columns.
claims.quote: The SDK supports create, update, and delete (CUD) of custom tables and columns

claims.claim: The SDK provides structured error handling.
claims.quote: Error handling: structured exception hierarchy with detailed error context and retry guidance.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging is opt-in and writes all HTTP requests and responses to a file.
claims.quote: HTTP diagnostics logging: opt-in file-based logging of all HTTP requests and responses

claims.claim: HTTP diagnostics logging redacts sensitive headers such as authorization.
claims.quote: with automatic redaction of sensitive headers, such as authorization.

claims.claim: The SDK internally calls the Dataverse Web API.
claims.quote: The SDK provides a Python programming interface that internally calls the Dataverse Web API.

claims.claim: Authentication uses an Azure Identity credential supplied to the SDK.
claims.quote: The SDK client requires any Azure Identity TokenCredential implementation for OAuth authentication with Dataverse.

claims.claim: The roadmap names autonomous data agents, form prediction and autofill, MCP and A2A as possible capabilities.
claims.quote:
Key capabilities can include:

- Autonomous data agents that can query, update, and evaluate data quality
- Form prediction and autofill
- Support for agentic primitives like Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) collaboration

claims.claim: The overview's feature list does not name autonomous data agents, form prediction and autofill, MCP or A2A.
claims.quote: Searched: read the entire sdk-python/overview feature list for autonomous data agents, form prediction, autofill, MCP and A2A; none is named. The overview does describe agentic workflows generally.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; summary; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Dataverse security roles govern SDK data operations rather than a separate SDK permission model.
claims.quote: Role-based access control: Enforces Dataverse security roles and policies for all data operations.

claims.claim: The SDK accesses existing Dataverse storage rather than introducing a new data store.
claims.quote: The Dataverse SDK for Python enables Python developers to interact directly with Microsoft Dataverse. You can easily access, manage, and manipulate data stored in Dataverse

claims.claim: Extracted copies of data outside Dataverse are no longer protected by its security boundary.
claims.quote: However, after the data has been extracted it is no longer protected by the security boundary provided by Dynamics 365 (online) and is instead controlled directly by the customer.

claims.claim: The getting-started example lists InteractiveBrowserCredential and AzureCliCredential as development options.
claims.quote:
# Development options
credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication
# credential = AzureCliCredential()

claims.claim: The getting-started example lists ClientSecretCredential and CertificateCredential as production options.
claims.quote:
# Production options
# credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)
# credential = CertificateCredential(tenant_id, client_id, cert_path)

claims.claim: The credential supplied determines whether authentication uses a user or an application identity.
claims.quote:
credential = InteractiveBrowserCredential()  # Browser authentication
# credential = ClientSecretCredential(tenant_id, client_id, client_secret)

claims.claim: InteractiveBrowserCredential accepts a client_id.
claims.quote:
client_id | str

Client ID of the Microsoft Entra application that users will sign into.

claims.claim: Without client_id, InteractiveBrowserCredential authenticates to an Azure development application.
claims.quote: If not specified, users will authenticate to an Azure development application, which is not recommended for production scenarios.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: client.files.upload automatically creates a missing file column as a permanent schema change.
claims.quote: If the file column doesn't exist, the SDK creates it automatically. Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table, and the new column becomes a permanent part of your environment's schema.

claims.claim: Changing table metadata requires customization privileges.
claims.quote: Creating a column is a metadata change: you need privileges to customize the table

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises creating file columns in advance in production.
claims.quote: In production environments, create file columns in advance rather than relying on automatic creation.

claims.claim: Running dataverse-install-claude-skill after package installation optionally installs Claude skills.
claims.quote:
you can optionally install two Claude Skills when installing the SDK from a package.

pip install PowerPlatform-Dataverse-Client && dataverse-install-claude-skill

claims.claim: The two installed skills have definition files on the developer's computer.
claims.quote: you can find skill definitions in the .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-use/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/dataverse-sdk-dev/SKILL.md files on your development computer.

claims.claim: The SDK retries operations after temporary failures such as throttling.
claims.quote: Automatic retries | Handle networking problems that might occur for operations that fail due to temporary problems, such as API throttling or service unavailability.

claims.claim: Dataverse service protection limits apply to external web service requests, including SDK traffic.
claims.quote: Service protection limits apply to all external web service requests, not only the CRUD operations on tables counted against entitlement limits.

claims.claim: Heavy scripts can affect other callers sharing the same user account because service protection is measured per user account and connection.
claims.quote: We limit the number of concurrent connections per user account, the number of API requests per connection, and the amount of execution time that can be used for each connection.

claims.claim: The getting-started page requires read/write access to a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: Read/write access to a Dataverse environment. You can use a trial environment.

claims.claim: OAuth authentication configured for the application is a prerequisite.
claims.quote: OAuth authentication configured for your application.

claims.claim: Network access to PyPI is an installation prerequisite.
claims.quote: Network access to https://pypi.org to obtain the SDK packages.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The SDK getting-started prerequisites and SDK pages do not name a Microsoft user or application licence requirement.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse access API user license application user Power Apps licensing Python SDK. Read SDK overview, get-started, quick-guide-dataverse and architecture prerequisites; no caller licence named there. General OAuth documentation does address licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because the SDK pages do not publish which entitlement covers callers.
claims.quote:
that user account needs a paid license. Don't use this approach.

In these cases, create a special application user that is bound to a Microsoft Entra ID registered application.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and replace the open-ended caller-licensing wording with: 'The SDK is open source; existing Dataverse entitlements still apply. Microsoft documents that using an ordinary user's credentials for an unattended app requires a paid licence, while an application user bound to a registered app does not consume a paid licence.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authenticate-oauth. Where a named product licence is needed, https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/maker/data-platform/data-platform-entity-licenses states that custom tables can be created with a Dynamics 365, Power Apps or Power Automate licence. Keep the narrower statement that the SDK pages name no SDK-specific Microsoft licence.

claims.claim: Dataverse CRUD, assign and share operations from SDK traffic count toward request limits like other clients and endpoints.
claims.quote: All create, read, update, and delete (CRUD), assign, and share operations including user-driven and internal system requests required to complete CRUD transactions

claims.claim: Application, non-interactive, administrative and system users share a non-licensed tenant-level request pool.
claims.quote:
These limits are defined and pooled at the tenant level.

Application users
Non-interactive users
Administrative users
SYSTEM user

claims.claim: No SDK-specific meter or charge is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse SDK Python tenant environment enable disable admin setting switch licensing price meter; "Dataverse" "Python" "SDK" "meter". Read SDK overview/get-started, capacity-storage and api-request-limits-allocations; only general capacity and request rules found.

claims.claim: Writing rows and files consumes Dataverse storage capacity.
claims.quote: In the Usage per storage type tile, you can view the consumption of your database, log, and file storage. This section displays your prepaid entitled capacity along with the corresponding usage.

claims.claim: App access control is at Security > Identity and access > App access control > environment > Set up app access control > Access control.
claims.quote:
select Security.
select Identity and access.
select App access control.
Select the environment
Select the Set up app access control button.
Select Enabled in the Access control dropdown list.

claims.claim: pac env list-settings --environment <environment-url> --filter application is the automation accompanying the app-access configuration control.
claims.quote:
pac env list-settings

List environment settings

Use the pac env update-settings command to change the values for some of these settings.
claims.fix: Replace the read call with 'pac env update-settings --environment <environment-url> --name applicationbasedaccesscontrolmode --value <mode>' and set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/env#pac-env-update-settings. Replace the read-only note with 'Changes the environment app-access-control mode, not the individual app allow/block lists.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/organization#BKMK_ApplicationBasedAccessControlMode for the writable setting. Do not hard-code an enabled/audit numeric value: that reference's description and choice labels disagree.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: App access control requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: The app-access-control prerequisites name Power Platform admin or Dynamics 365 admin.
claims.quote:
Verify your role

There are two Power Platform related service admin roles you can assign

Power Platform admin
Dynamics 365 admin

claims.claim: App access control does not apply to partner apps making service-to-service calls.
claims.quote:
Client app access control isn't applied to the following apps:

First-party apps with service-to-service calls (application context)

Partner apps with service-to-service calls

claims.claim: Application users are configured through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user.
claims.quote:
Select + New app user to open the Create a new app user pane.
Select + Add an app to choose the registered Microsoft Entra application
claims.fix: The printed route is correct but stops at the creation pane. Extend it to 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > + Add an app'. Add to the note: 'Choose the app and business unit, then use the security-roles edit icon to select the new user's roles.'

claims.claim: The versioned addAppUser POST with servicePrincipalAppId creates a Dataverse application user.
claims.quote: POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01
claims.fix: Print only 'POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01' in api.call and add 'The request body sets servicePrincipalAppId to the registered app's client ID' to the note.

claims.claim: The create-application-user API documentation is marked preview.
claims.quote:
Create a Dataverse application user (preview)

[This article is pre-release documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The addAppUser API always adds the application user as System Administrator.
claims.quote: This always adds the application user as a System Administrator.

claims.claim: Environment auditing is at Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
claims.quote:
select Security > Compliance.
Select the Auditing tile.
Select the environment that you want to turn on auditing.
Select Set up auditing. In the Auditing pane, select Turn on auditing.

claims.claim: The GET organizations query is the automation accompanying the control for whether Dataverse records changes and access.
claims.quote:
Retrieve organization settings

Use the following queries to retrieve your organization settings.

Change organization settings

Change the column values in the organization table to change how auditing works for the environment.
claims.fix: Replace api.call with 'PATCH [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations([Organization ID])'. Replace 'The call reads the settings' with 'The request body sets isauditenabled to enable environment auditing and isuseraccessauditenabled for user-access logging.' Keep the existing table/column-auditing qualification and the same docs URL.

claims.claim: Changing auditing settings requires System Administrator or System Customizer.
claims.quote: Anyone can view the configuration, but you must have the System Administrator or System Customizer role to change the settings.

claims.claim: Recording changes requires environment, table and column auditing to be enabled.
claims.quote: First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.claim: Environment auditing alone does not enable user-access logging; Log access is required.
claims.quote:
IsUserAccessAuditEnabled ... Whether user access logging is enabled
Auditing for the environment must be enabled for user access logging to be enabled.
